chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one in Ihram, when he catches a dove, then for it is a sheep; and if he kills its chicks, then for it is a lamb; and if he tramples the egg, then upon him is a Dirham.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: A Dirham (silver coin, used as a unit of value)
key_terms.شَاةٌ: A sheep (used as a unit of value/expiation)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing a dove or its eggs while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific fidyah (expiation) for a pilgrim in Ihram who kills or damages birds, distinguishing between catching a dove, killing its chicks, or trampling its eggs. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving precise legal rulings from the Imams, linking the severity of the act to the value of the compensation, such as a sheep or a dirham. This ruling is part of the broader jurisprudence of Hajj, ensuring that the sanctity of the sacred state is maintained through tangible restitution.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one in Ihraam, when he attains a dove, so with regards to it is a sheep; and if he kills a chick, so regarding it is a lamb, and if he tramples the egg, so upon him is a Dirham’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn ‘ Abd Allah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one in the state of Ihram kills a pigeon, the ransom for it is one sheep, if he kill its chick its ransom is one lamb, and if he steps on its egg its ransom is one dirham.’”
